Above analysis establishes a complete systematic test scheme for the high resistance grounding fault detection, and provides an effective test support for the subsequent effectual fault detection method for high resistance grounding fault.

articleTitle: A New Principle of DC Distribution Line Over-Current Protection for Solid-State Transformer Based on Current Derivative
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: As the key equipment of AC-DC hybrid distribution network, the protection and fault isolation of solid-state transformers (SSTs) are of great significance. When the DC distribution line short circuit fault occurs, the fault current rises very fast. According to the structure of solid-state transformer, this paper analyzes the DC distribution line fault, which has two stages: RLC resonance and inductor current free-wheeling. Based on this, a protection method using transient current mutation is proposed, which can quickly identify faults and protect DC lines by using the concavity and convexity of the current waveform. The simulation of DC distribution line fault of solid-state transformer by PSCAD/EMTDC verifies the correctness of theoretical analysis and practicability of the proposed protection method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Governor’s Dead Band on Frequency Stability of System Based on Describing Function method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Ultra-low frequency oscillations caused by the governor of power system occur in actual power systems recent years. In addition, Governor's dead band also introduces nonlinear link to the system and make it more difficult to analyzing the frequency stability of power system. In this paper, the influences of non-step dead band and step dead band on frequency oscillation are analyzed with the describing function method in the single-machine system. The locus of minus reciprocal of the describing function of dead band with oscillation amplitude, and the locus of open-loop transform function with oscillation frequency are plotted on the complex plane. According to the Nyquist stability criterion, The relative location of the two loci determines system stability. When the minus reciprocal locus entirely locates on the left of the open-loop frequency characteristic locus, the system is stable. Furthermore, The non-step dead band and step dead band can change the frequency stability of system when the system is unstable without dead band. Results of the time-domain simulations validate the conclusion.

articleTitle: Measurement Error Detection of Electric Power Meter Based on Least Square Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Huge amount current transformers and power meters are installed in the power system of the Spaceflight Launch Site, and how to find the abnormal ones with large measurement deviation in time is a key technology to ensure the reliablity of the ground system. Using power balance theory between input circuits and output, we study the relationships of input-output difference, construct the error prediction model, which is predicted through the least square model. The experimental result based on the real measurement data shows the effectiveness of our model.

articleTitle: Automatic Switchover System Scheme for 20kV Petal-shape Distribution Network Non-communication Protection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Automatic bus transfer equipment is one of the most effective means to improve the power supply reliability of power system.At present, few domestic 20kV "petal shaped" distribution network operation has considered the use of automatic switching function,So it will extend part of the load power outage time. This paper has improved a automatic switchover system scheme for 20kV "petal" type distribution network which without channel protection. Through coordination of the settle time of the distribution line which between non-channel protection and automatic bus transfer, under the condition that there is no breakdown of the connecting generatrix of the tie ring network switch,except for the longest cutoff time tset,any single phase voltage is below the set voltage and automatic bus transfer can be fast input.Simulation verification by PSCAD/EMTDC,this scheme can effectively improve the reliability and self-healing of the system, and shorten the outage time of the users.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Method of Jiles-Atherton Hysteresis Model Based on Parameter Identification of Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The accurate description of the magnetization hysteresis characteristics for ferromagnetic materials which are the core components of important power equipment such as power transformers produces vital significance for the safety and stability control of equipment. In this paper, aiming at the problem that the differential permeability of the local hysteresis loop is not accord with the physical reality in the Jiles-Atherton hysteresis model. An improved hysteresis model based on genetic algorithm parameter identification is proposed to resolve the problem. The comparison of the simulation and test results for hysteresis characteristics shows high accuracy of the proposed model and confirms the effectiveness of the algorithm. Meanwhile, the accuracy of the local hysteresis loop characteristics of the model is effectively enhanced, which provides an exact model basis for further study of the residual magnetic properties of the power transformer core.

articleTitle: A Conventional Distance Protection for Series-Compensated Lines Considering TCSC Protected by a Metal Oxide Varistor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In this paper, a modified distance protection setting method is proposed to use the conventional distance relays for the transmission lines. The comprehensive studies regarding the impact of the thyristor-controlled series capacitor (TCSC) on a conventional distance relay are shown that the TCSC affects the operation of distance relays not only at the series compensated lines but also at the adjacent lines. The proposed method uses the equivalent impedance of the TCSC considering a metal oxide varistor (MOV), which is one of the overvoltage protection element for the TCSC to calculate the setting values which can prevent the mal-operation of the distance relays. To analyze and evaluate the performance of proposed method, a series of simulation studies were carried out with the PSS/E and PSCAD/EMTDC environment.

articleTitle: Research and development of traveling wave monitoring device for nanosecond precision ground fault based on 4G Data Transfer Unit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To solve the problem of limiting the accuracy of double-end traveling wave ranging by the existing traveling wave monitoring device, a traveling wave monitoring device for nanosecond time-precision grounding fault based on 4G DTU is developed. Firstly, the high-speed data acquisition card and DSP, is used to collect, analyze and storage fault voltage. Then the GPS nanosecond timing module is used to calculate the voltage reference time. Finally, 4G DTU is used to send fault data to the background computer. This paper introduces the method of collecting and storing fault voltage data and calculating voltage reference time of the device. The debugging results show that the data acquisition, analysis and transmission functions meet the requirements of the online monitoring device, and the fault voltage reference time accuracy calculated by the device is nanosecond, and the fault data can be used for subsequent fault location work.

articleTitle: An Improved Control Method for Voltage Source Converter-High Voltage Direct Current System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper aims to enhance the accuracy and response speed of the active-disturbance rejection control (ADRC) controller of the voltage source converter-high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) system. For this purpose, an improved control method was proposed for the VSC-HVDC system based on the least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) optimization of the ADRC controller. First, the ADRC regulators were designed for the active/reactive power outer loop in VSC-HVDC inverter control system. Then, the LSSVM optimized regression model was created for the ADRC regulators. Finally, the proposed method was successfully simulated on MATLAB. The simulation results show that the LSSVM-optimized ADRC method can effectively enhance the anti-interference ability of the VSC-HVDC. The research findings shed new light on the signal analysis of the VSC-HVDC system.

Author Keywords: Voltage Source Converter-High Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC)

articleTitle: Control Scheme of Y-connected Modular Multilevel Converter in Fractional Frequency Transmission System Under Unbalanced Grid Fault
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Y-connected modular multilevel converter (Y-MMC) is a new topology of direct AC/AC power conversion, with competitive application prospects in Fractional Frequency Transmission System (FFTS). To improve the uninterrupted operation capability of Y-MMC, the control strategy considering unbalanced grid fault is proposed in this paper. This paper proposes the mathematical model of Y-MMC under asymmetric grid conditions according to the symmetrical component method and superposition principle of linear systems. Based on the proposed mathematical model, positive and negative sequence current inner loop controller, and outer loop controller to suppress the negative sequence current are specially designed for the stable operation of Y-MMC under asymmetric grid conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy has been verified by the simulation results obtained from a 10 kV, 10 MW Y-MMC system built in MATLAB /Simulink.

articleTitle: Personal safety analysis of live working in 10kV distribution network based on finite element method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In order to reduce the power outage time caused by the maintenance and replacement of equipment on the transmission line, live working is widely used in the operation and maintenance of distribution network in China. Because the line is in a live operation state in this mode of operation, the operators are under potential safety risks on the line. In the event of an accident, their personal safety is threatened. In this paper, the electric shock mechanism of 10kV distribution network under live operation is studied. The simulation software Ansys/Maxwell is used to build the distribution network line and tower model. The electric field strength and potential distribution of the charged working space and the operator's body surface are analyzed based on finite element method.

articleTitle: Research on Traveling Wavefront Identification Method Based on the Dominant Frequency Component of Full Waveform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Traveling wavefront identification accuracy and wave speed selection precision are crucial to traveling wave location. Aiming at the two issues, the method based on the dominant frequency component of full waveform is proposed. At first, the time-frequency characteristic is studied by full waveforms of the traveling wave, especially the frequency-dependent characteristic of wave speed and wavefront attenuation. Second, according to the criterion of the maximum energy, the dominant frequency component can be extracted from all frequency components and the corresponding wave speed is calculated. Finally, Teager Energy Operation (TEO) is introduced to enhance the transient feature of the dominant frequency component in order to precisely determine traveling wavefront the arrival time. The simulation results show that the traveling wavefront identification performance based on the proposed method is pretty to meet the fault location requirement. Also, the proposed method is adaptive under different fault conditions.

articleTitle: Passive Circuit Model Construction and Application on the Key Structure of Converter Valve
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For long distance and large capacity transmission problems, high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission is a suggestive alternative. In the design and construction process of HVDC transmission project, analysis on overvoltage and resonance characteristic of key equipment is indispensable. This paper employs a method to construct a passive broadband model for the converter valve. The Vector Fitting (VF) method is adopted to get a fitting curve with frequency impedances measured off at hundreds of sample points. Afterwards, the corresponding passive equivalent broadband circuit is built via passive algorithm and synthesis procedure. The applicability of the method to our model is confirmed by comparing the simulated and measured data. The double exponential model parameters of overvoltage are calculated according to the definition of International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the voltage distribution of the valve module composed of the key components is characterized, in favor of which the key components can be optimized.

articleTitle: Precise Locating Method of Generator Stator Grounding Fault Point Based on Injected Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In view of the difficulty and low accuracy of stator grounding fault location for large generators, a method for accurate stator grounding fault location based on neutral injection signal is presented in this paper. Inject Non-power-frequency current signal into the stator neutral point during shutdown. The branch current is measured at the head and end of the fault phase branch. The fault branch is detected by the current difference comparison method at the head and end of the branch. The coil measurement point in the sub-fault branch is set by the dichotomy method to accurately locate the fault point to the slot number. The principle of adjusting current limiting resistance to improve detection accuracy is analyzed. The method can significantly improve the accuracy of stator grounding fault location. This way can reduce the downtime and effectively increase the efficiency of stator grounding fault treatment.

articleTitle: Study on High Impedance Grounding Fault Protection for Personal Safety Guard in Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In recent years, human electric shock accident caused by line fault of distribution system has happened all over the world. This kind of problem of high resistance grounding fault safety is becoming more and more the attention of the researchers. In this paper, typical arc high resistance grounding fault model is established to simulate the human electric shock accident and the line fell to the ground condition. The transient- state and steady-state fault characteristics of high resistance grounding fault are analyzed in the neutral point grounded through a small resistance grounding system and the resonant grounding system. The above analysis has laid a good foundation for the establishment of an effective fault detection method for high resistance grounding and the realization of human electric shock protection.

articleTitle: Analysis of DFIG Terminal Voltage Oscillation Caused by Reactive Power Compensation under Weak Grid Connection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: According to the wind farm codes, the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) is required to possess low voltage ride through (LVRT) capability during grid faults, especially reactive power compensation performance. However, under weak grid connected condition, the interaction between DFIG control system and grid may cause voltage oscillations at the point of common coupling (PCC). To investigate the mechanism of the oscillation phenomenon during LVRT, this paper establishes a reactive power compensation equivalent model, considering system transient characteristics, weak grid structure and rotor-side converter (RSC) controllers. The results of Nyquist criterion confirm that the transient stability of wind power system will be deteriorated with the increase of compensation gain value and grid impedance. A DFIG simulation model is built to verify the validity of the model and theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Ubiquitous Power Internet of Things Architecture Construction Plan
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In order to effectively realize the construction of Ubiquitous Power Internet of Things, a communication technology architecture plan for the construction of sensing layer and the network layer is proposed, the idea of optimizing energy allocation is also proposed in the plan. The aim of the plan is to solve the data sensing and interaction problems of household electrical appliances, distribution network equipment, factories and so on, the plan also attributes to solving the load data transmission and interaction problems. The idea of intelligent power consumption is also put forward in the article.

Author Keywords: smart networking technology of electric appliances

articleTitle: Fault disappearing judgement of single phase grounding in neutral point non-effective grounding system based on adjustable resistor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In the distribution network, it is important to determine whether single phase grounding fault has disappeared in time. The reason is that accurate determination contribute to improving safety of system operation and reliability of power supply. This paper proposed a method to judge the disappearance of single phase ground fault based on neutral point non-effective grounding system by means of adjustable resistor. When single phase grounding occurs, forcibly grounding the fault phase at the busbar could reduce fault point voltage and reduce high residual voltage hazard. Then adjust the value of adjustable resistor at the busbar grounding branch, and then monitor the trend of grounding branch current to determine if the fault has disappeared. Simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately and timely judge whether single phase grounding fault disappears.

articleTitle: Study on Operation Characteristics of Wind Power Grid-connected Doubly-Fed AC/DC Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Aiming at the impact of large-scale wind power integration on the operation characteristics of HVDC, this paper builds an AC-DC hybrid double-fed HVDC system including wind power generation. In the PSCAD/EMTDC software, the steady-state and transient operation characteristics of wind power access system are studied. The results show that the system can reach stable operation within 0.2s when the system starts. When the three-phase short-circuit ground fault occurs, the DC voltage and active power of the system show a downward trend, after the 0.05 s fault removal, active power of line gradually restores stability under the action of regulator, but line voltage appears unstable. When one end is disconnected, the voltage and active power on the fault side change to zero instantaneously, and the other end has a small reduction, and then it can resume normal operation.

articleTitle: Short-term Load Forecasting Model Based on Attention Mechanism and Gated Recurrent Unit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Short-term load forecasting (STLF) is an important task for the stable and economic operation of power systems. However, the existing STLF methods are incapable of fitting the time series and nonlinear characteristics of load data simultaneously or cannot take into account the different influences from various input features on the predicted load values, so the improvement of the accuracy in STLF is limited seriously. To address these problems, an optimized STLF model called Attention-GRU is proposed in this paper. The proposed model not only employs gated recurrent unit (GRU) to accommodate the time series and nonlinear characteristics of load data, but also highlights the critical features through attention mechanism. By using an actual dataset from Australia to implement experiments, the results show that the proposed model outperforms the baseline models based on back propagation (BP) neural network, long short-term memory (LSTM) and GRU in term of forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Field Test Method for DC Protection Equipment of HVDC by Secondary Signal Simulating
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The field test for these has not been implemented regularly due to lacking simple and feasible method. This paper proposed a novel field test method for DC protection equipment of HVDC by secondary signal simulating with low security risk and low cost. It is not need to remove the equipment and explain the photoelectric conversion protocol. The field test device for DC protection equipment of HVDC has been developed. This device has secondary signal simulation ability of optical current transformer and zero flux current transformer. The field test device for DC protection equipment of HVDC has been developed with secondary signal simulation ability of optical current transformer and zero flux current transformer. Its validity was verified by field testing of DC protection equipment in Jiangling-Echeng ±500kV HVDC project. This project has been in operation more than ten years.

articleTitle: SMA based Reduced-order Model for DFIGs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: As the integration of wind power increases in the power system, it is the basic requirement to model wind generators properly for the power system stability analysis and transient simulation. In this paper, a reduced-order method based on selective modal analysis (SMA) is proposed for constructing a reduced model of DFIGs. The whole system model with DFIGs is introduced firstly. Then the reduced-order method using SMA is presented in detailed about how to constructing a reduced model using the key modes and participate factors from the modal analysis. The comparison between the detailed model and the reduced model is carried out in the theoretical analysis and the transient simulation. Both the theoretical and simulation results verify that the reduced-order model can well fit the original steady and transient behavior of the system, which significantly reduces the computational complexity and thus improves the efficiency.

articleTitle: Fault Phase Identification Method Based on Convolutional Neural Network for Double Circuit Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In order to address the problems that model-driven distance protection cannot correctly identify the fault phases when it is applied to the DCTL (double circuit transmission lines on the same tower), a fault phase identification method based on CNN (convolutional neural network) is proposed. The method only needs to input the current and voltage waveforms under different fault types into the CNN. The CNN automatically extracts the characteristics of the waveform, and the fault types finally are identified based on the extracted characteristics. The performance of the proposed method is verified by a larger number of fault data. The test results show that the proposed method can effectively identify the fault phases of the DCTL.

Author Keywords: double circuit transmission lines on the same tower

articleTitle: The Experiences of Decentralized Self-Healing Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper describes the experiences of deploying distribution ring network self-healing control system in China, including the architecture designing, retrofitting with advanced controller, simulating and testing on site.This decentralized self-healing system consists of nine sets of edging controllers Easergy T300 installed on 20kV feeders. These modular-designed T300s are fully integrated into ring main unit (RMU) switches. It is important specially for existing RMU upgrading that extra space is not needed.These controllers are connected using peer to peer (P2P) communication to build an autonomous system. The principle of the self-healing grid automation system is to start an automatic sequence of re-energizing the healthy part of the MV ring after a short circuit or earth fault somewhere in the ring. The re-energizing operations have to be performed in a minimum time with a maximum of safety and security. No distribution management system (DMS) is required and no operator intervention is needed.To validate this decentralized self-healing system, there are two steps: in the lab, special test bench can verify the whole system which is almost same as a real system just except communication network; on site, a dedicated simulator can be used to "generate" a short circuit fault, then switches are operated automatically according to self-healing algorithm in the real communication network.The project was implemented for State Grid Corporation of China. The main objectives of this program are to improve the feeder automation capability and enhance reliability of power supply in the CBD area of Hangzhou. This self-healing control system help our utility customer to achieve their goals.

articleTitle: A Study on the Influence of Three-phase Unbalance of AC Side Voltage on on the Operating Characteristics of VSC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of the AC three-phase voltage unbalance problem in the low-voltage distribution network on the operating characteristics of the VSC is studied. This paper deduces the expression of the negative sequence component of the three-phase unbalanced voltage after park transformation and develops the simulation model of the low-voltage DC distribution network. The correctness of the theoretical derivation is verified by simulation. The simulations of three-phase unbalances of 5%, 10%, and 15% were performed to investigate the effects of different three-phase unbalance on DC voltage. The results show that the three-phase voltage imbalance on the AC side will introduce a double-frequency voltage component on the DC side. The greater the voltage imbalance, the larger the amplitude of the introduced double-frequency voltage component, and the more serious the impact on the DC voltage quality.

articleTitle: Power Electronic Switching Models for Numerical Simulations of Power System Electromagnetic Transient
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Due to the increasing number of power electronic devices in modern power systems in the past two decades, the numerical simulation results of electromechanical transient processes based on quasi-steady state models have been questioned under critical operating mode. Therefore, it is urgent to develop software for electromagnetic transient simulation of real power systems. One of the most difficult problems in this study is how to set up a suitable power electronic switching model. This paper reviews relative research literatures on mathematical models of power electronic switches without considering their own transient processes, introduces the establishment methods of various models and their applications in widely used commercial software, and evaluates their advantages and disadvantages.

articleTitle: HVDC Startup Strategy in AC/DC Hybrid System Black Start Process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Reducing the power system restoration time has always been an important topic in power system research. For AC/DC hybrid systems, if the rapid regulation ability of HVDC is utilized in the early stage of black start, the restoration time can be reduced. This paper proposes a HVDC startup strategy while considering HVDC lines and explores their control flexibility in the black start process. The requirement on the minimum short-circuit ratio (SCR) is presented based on the concept of critical short-circuit ratio (CSCR) under non-rated state. The maximum transmittable power of HVDC is obtained using the short-circuit ratio of the system. The feasibility of the proposed HVDC startup strategy is proved through numerical simulation on the IEEE 24-bus test system and the black-start scheme that including HVDC startup can significantly reduce the system restoration time.

articleTitle: Line Protection Scheme for MMC-based Multiterminal DC Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For flexible medium-voltage DC distribution grid, this paper proposes a DC line protection method. Frist, characteristic differences of transient current variation at both ends of the line are analyzed when fault occurs. Afterwards a line protection scheme is proposed based on initial current travelling wave. Through comparing the polarity of current modulus maxima at both ends of the line, the method can identify the internal and external faults. A modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based multi-terminal DC distribution grid is constructed using PSCAD/EMTDC, and extensive simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. Simulation results show that the proposed protection method can detect the fault section rapidly and accurately.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of AC-DC Hybrid Grid Based on State Enumeration Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: DC grid, which is more suitable for the integration of intermittent energy, should undergo a reliability evaluation before being put into production. This paper proposes the reliability model for AC-DC converter and DC-DC converter firstly. Then, a minimum load shedding model considering the interaction between AC grid, HVDC and DC grid is presented. Finally, based on the state enumeration, the reliability evaluation for the AC-DC hybrid grid is accomplished. The results show that moderate redundant SM and the reduction of IGBT and capacitance failure rate can significantly improve the reliability of the AC-DC hybrid gird.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Assessment Method of Distribution Network with Distributed Generation Based on Latin Hypercube Sampling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the access of distributed generation (DG), the structure of distribution network will be changed. Due to intermittent and randomness of the output of DG, it will bring risk to distribution system. In order to realize risk quantitative assessment of distribution network with DG, the outage model of DG and other component of distribution network are built firstly. Second, Latin hypercube sampling method which has smaller variance and faster convergence is proposed to sample and sort the system states. Then a risk assessment process with island isolation of distribution network with DG is proposed. According to the sampling result, the risk indexes are calculated and the risk level classification criteria is proposed in the paper. Finally, the rationality and effectiveness of blackout risk assessment method is verified with IEEE 39-bus distribution network. The simulation results show that the proposed method has smaller variance and faster convergence.

articleTitle: Influence of Off-shore Wind Farm on Power System Small-Signal Stability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the gradual exhaustion of fossil fuel, development of the off-shore wind power becomes very important in Guangdong province. This paper is focused on the impacts of the increasing penetration of wind farm on power system small-signal stability. Simulation results show that the oscillation mode is related to the penetration of wind farm. Different kinds of wind turbine models are considered. Simulation results show that the detailed wind turbine model brings new oscillation mode related to the wind turbine itself. This modeling method provides theoretical foundation and a tool for small signal stability analysis of the power system containing large scale off-shore wind farms.

articleTitle: A Discrete System Approach for Short-term Voltage Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: A key task in stability analysis is to solve a group of differential - algebraic equations. In this paper, a closed-form solution of the network equations is derived based on the familiar Dommel-Sato iteration. For different load models, we derive the corresponding closed-form network voltage expressions. After applying the improved Euler integration, a discrete system model of AC power grid dynamics is obtained. Examples using the proposed discrete system model are provided, and compared with the simulation results using BPA, a popular production-grade simulation software.

articleTitle: Fault Location Method for Seafloor Observation Network Based on Multi-terminal Traveling Wave Time Difference
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Currently, fault detection and location of submarine cable in seafloor observation network is affected by fault resistance, natural environment and climate. The seafloor observation network's submarine cable failure is difficult to detect and locate, thus bringing many obstacles to underwater maintenance. Aiming at the defects of current fault location methods in seafloor observation network, a fault location method based on multi-terminal traveling wave is proposed for the first time in this paper. Firstly, the fault line is determined with intelligent branch unit (BU), and the shortest transmission path of the initial fault traveling wave head is calculated with Floyd algorithm. Secondly, the submarine cable is divided into several equipartition sections, and the distances from each equipartition point to each line end point and connecting point are calculated. Then an initial traveling wave path matrix is constructed, and the reference traveling wave head arrival time difference matrix is established based on the traveling wave velocity. After the fault, a time difference matrix is established using the times the traveling wave heads arrive at the fault point, measured with the synchronous measuring device installed at the end of each line. Finally, the fault location is determined using the difference of the time difference matrix before and after the fault. PSCAD simulation proves that the proposed method is simple to implement and accurate in positioning, providing guarantee for safe and reliable operation of the submarine observation network power system.

articleTitle: Small Signal Stability Analysis and Control Optimization of Y-connected Modular Multilevel Converter for Fractional Frequency Offshore Wind Power Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Y-connected modular multilevel converter(Y-MMC) is a new circuit topology of direct AC/AC power conversion, with competitive application prospects in fractional frequency offshore wind power system. Different from the previous converter topology, Y-MMC realizes the frequency conversion by single-phase voltage cancellation. Simultaneously, the voltages between main bridges and auxiliary bridges can be determined by the reactive power distribution coefficients. Considering the frequency leakage problem, this paper proposes the new mathematical model of Y-MMC and builds corresponding control strategy. Then, the state equation of the system and its small-signal models are established, the small distribution stability is analyzed. Furthermore, to improve the stability and dynamic performance of the closed-loop control system, the parameters of controller are optimized based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed control strategies are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Study on Suppression Measures for Voltage over-limit of Distribution Network With Small Hydropower Group
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Small hydropower groups connected to the distribution network and operated in reverse power state will cause voltage over-limit in the key nodes and some nodes of grid. Through the analysis of the power system voltage regulation principle, four voltage regulation measures such as adjusting the generator voltage, changing the transformer ratio, performing reactive power compensation, and optimizing the conductor are obtained. Taking a regional distribution network as an example, based on the PSASP (Power System Analysis Software Package) simulation software, a distribution network model with small hydropower groups was established, focusing on the distribution line voltage of the distribution network in the reverse power state during the summer flood season. The four voltage regulation measures were simulated under voltage over-limit, which effects of suppression methods were analyzed and compared. It has certain reference significance and engineering practical value for the voltage adjustment of hydropower access distribution network in the future.

articleTitle: An Identification Method for Sympathetic Inrush Based on Substation-Area Information
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Sympathetic inrush is a phenomenon that occurs in an in-service transformer (IT) when a nearby transformer is energized. The phenomenon can cause transformer differential protection to maloperate. Identification methods for sympathetic inrush have been proposed to deal with the problem. However, these methods are based on local information from the IT, while sympathetic inrush involves two or more transformers. Therefore, an identification method is proposed based on substation-area information. A substation-area differential current is defined and its second harmonic component is utilized to identify the sympathetic inrush. Simulation results by PSCAD/EMTDC show the proposed method can distinguish sympathetic inrush from internal faults and energization inrush effectively.

articleTitle: An Improved Frequency Estimation Method Without Iterations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The frequency estimation solutions based on the discrete phase locked loop (PLL) technology are widely applied in the intelligence electronic devices for power system. The PLL method cannot provide both the fast response and the good reliability under the system disturbance. In this paper, an improved frequency estimation solution is presented. Based on the angle characteristic of the positive sequence voltage, this method directly calculates the frequency deviation from angle difference of the continuous power cycles, without any iteration calculation. Unlike the discrete phase locked loop, which is a close-loop structure, the new method is based on an open-loop structure with the fixed sampling frequency. There is no interdependent between the calculation loops. Hence, the response time is shorter. Moreover, the 2 cycles hamming window is applied to reduce the interfaces and the angle jump detection based on the abnormal rate of change of frequency is also applied to improve the reliability of the solution. The theoretical analysis and Matlab simulations are performed. The results show the frequency estimation performance can meet the application requirements.

articleTitle: Coordination Control of Battery Energy Storage and MTGS in An Independent AC Micro-grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: In the independent ac micro-grid system, the coordination control between MTGS and battery energy storage is the key to ensure the stable operation of the system. A coordinated control method is proposed based on the quick response of battery. In view of the voltage quality problem when the main power supply in the micro grid is converted from the energy storage system to the micro gas turbine or from the micro gas turbine to the energy storage system, this paper proposes a seamless switching control strategy for the dual main power supply of the MTGS and the energy storage battery. Finally, PSCAD simulation software is used to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: SREKF Based State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: State of health (SOH) estimation plays an important role in battery management system. This problem is addressed by introducing a second-order RC equivalent circuit model (ECM) and square root extended kalman filter (SREKF) in this work. According to the ECM, the ohmic resistance (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) which represents the SOH is molded as a state vector, and lithium battery SOH is obtained by using the internal relationship between ohm resistance and SOH. Then the state of the resulting nonlinear dynamic system is estimated in real time by the SREKF which can guarantee the symmetry and non-negative characteristics of the state variance matrix by the square root method recursively. The verification results show that the SREKF algorithm can estimate the SOH parameter more accurately and reduce the maximum error of the ohmic resistance by 6% under 1C-rate constant current test compared with the EKF algorithm.

articleTitle: Assessment of Data Flow Control Methods and their Performance on IEC61850 based Digital Substation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Data flow control methods are deployed to avoid network traffic congestion and achieve the best data flow maximizing reliability and availability performance of the IEC 61850 based digital substation These methods include First in First out (FIFO), Priority Queuing (PQ), and Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ). This paper presents the substation automation system (SAS) performance evaluation and comparison studies for these three different data flow control methods. A National Grid (NG) typical 400kV substation is simulated by using OPNET Modeler, communication network simulation software. Three different data flow control methods are applied to the process bus and station bus in the substation respectively. The message (i.e. SV, GOOSE, MMS) delay, packet loss probability, and other network performance are investigated and analysed under different case scenarios. Results shows PQ control method has the best performance respect to time critical messages during the feeder fault conditions, followed by WFQ, and FIFO respectively. In addition, PQ has a smaller network delay than WFQ and FIFO. However, some packets with lower priority class can be delay even lost under traffic queuing condition. Therefore, the simulation results can be used to help power utilities and industries to improve and achieve the data flow management, also for substation expansion in the future.

articleTitle: A New Control Strategy for Capacitor Voltage Balance of Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) has become the most promising topology in flexible direct current transmission. However, the voltage ripple occurs to the submodule capacitor voltage in normal operation, which makes the loss increasing. To address this issue, this paper analyzes the mechanism of capacitor voltage ripple in a fundamental frequency period from the point of view of energy in detail. In addition, a new control strategy based on arm energy redistribution that can reduce the capacitor voltage ripple is proposed. Simulation results under normal operation based on Simulink/MATLAB prove the feasibility and validity of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Health Condition Assessment of Pole-mounted Switch Assemblies Based on Hybrid Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the continuous construction of distribution automation, the reliability of pole-mounted switch assemblies had been paid more and more attention. This paper presents a health condition assessment model based on multi-source data, using support vector regression (SVM), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) and Random Forest (RF). Firstly, the four single evaluation models are established. Then a hybrid algorithm evaluation model of four intelligent algorithms based on the four single evaluation models is established. And in order to optimize the results simulation a hybrid algorithm evaluation model of three intelligent algorithms which eliminating RF algorithm is built. According to the simulation results, the health condition assessment model synthesizing three intelligent algorithms is the best one. The results can be used in engineering practice to arrange the maintenance of the pole-mounted switch assemblies reasonably and improve the reliability of distribution system.

articleTitle: Study on Vibration Characteristics of Transformer Insulation Ageing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The fault caused by transformer insulation aging accounts for a large proportion of the total fault of the transformer. Therefore, it is extremely important to accurately evaluate the aging state of the transformer insulation. In this paper, the vibration characteristics of windings under different load currents and different pressing forces are studied. A transformer aging test platform was built in the laboratory. The vibration characteristics of the transformer tank surface under different aging times were studied by accelerated aging test. The results lay the foundation for transformer insulation aging evaluation technology based on vibration signal.

articleTitle: Location and analysis of partial discharge in GIS based on on-line monitoring and improved signal waveform feature method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Online monitoring technology is the real-time monitoring and fault pre-diagnosis of effective GIS technology, the time delay method is a major means of fixing the GIS partial discharge, which is based on the waveform feature points of time delay calculation method has been widely applied in the practical engineering, this paper to improve the signal waveform characteristic point, puts forward the feature points is replaced by a rising edge delay calculation method, through together based on uhf partial discharge phenomena found in the on-line monitoring system, the signal waveform feature points and rising along the method has carried on the comparative study. The research shows that compared with the signal waveform characteristic point method, the rising edge method not only improves the positioning accuracy, but also inherits the advantages of simple operation and low cost of signal waveform characteristic point method, which has certain engineering application value.

articleTitle: Analytical Analysis and Protection Setting of Taveling Wave Protection in Hybrid HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The hybrid HVDC system, in which the rectifier is made up of LCC and the converter is composed of MMC, has quite different characteristics from the symmetrical LCC-HVDC systems. Therefore, it is necessary to study the protection method for hybrid HVDC transmission lines. This paper develops a reduced analytical model of LCC-MMC-HVDC system for DC line fault transient analysis. The analytical models of internal and external fault are established in frequency domain and applicable to the first fault traveling wave. Analysis illustrates that it has high accuracy compared with the simulation result. Based on the reduced model, the analytical setting method of traveling wave protection is put forward, which considers the randomness of sampling. Furthermore, the performance of traveling wave protection is analyzed based on the analytical analysis, and the result shows that traveling wave protection performances well for the MMC side, but it has quite poor ability of resistance at LCC side of the transmission line.

articleTitle: Robust Unit Commitment in Integrated Electricity and Dynamic Natural Gas System Considering Gas Storage
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To overcome the difficulties caused by the uncertainty of renewable energy in solving the unit commitment in integrated electricity and natural gas system (IEGS), a robust optimization model is proposed in this paper, in which the dynamic and gas storage tanks of natural gas systems (NGS) are also considered. The time scales of power system (PS) and the NGS are different from each other, and the dynamic characteristics of NGS are remarkably slower than those of PS, so it is necessary to model the dynamic NGS and explore its benefits for the PS. Moreover, since the gas storage tanks can cope with the stochastic fluctuations caused by the gas load, it is necessary to consider the benefits of the gas storage tanks in IEGS. The model is applied to the IEEE 39-bus-15-node IEGS to verify its validity.

Author Keywords: integrated electricity and natural gas system

articleTitle: Research on DC Line Fault Recovery Sequence of Yongren-Funing HVDC Project
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Basic design of DC line fault restart principle of Yongren-Funing HVDC project is firstly introduced. Then the protection configuration and response characteristics of DC fault recovery is theoretically analyzed. Subsequently, a simulation model of Yongren-Funing HVDC is built in RTDS real-time environment. Simulation of the DC line fault and corresponding fault recovery is performed. Responses of the typical electrical quantities such as voltage, current and power in the rectifier and inverter side are analyzed. In addition, field experiments results are compared with the ones gets from the simulation. This comparison study validates the effectiveness of the control and protection system. Moreover, the fault restart principle meets the design requirement. as a result, the fault restart principle and protection configuration provide in this paper is useful to the design and operation of other newly-built HVDC projects.

articleTitle: Transformer Inrush Current Restraining Method Based on Integrated Control of Closing Voltage Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: On the basis of the mathematical relationship between transformer inrush current and closing voltage parameters, a scheme of suppress transformer inrush current is proposed based on the control of closing voltage amplitude and closing angle. This scheme adopts a combination of voltage amplitude control function and closing angle, which control target is the magnetic flux does not exceed the saturation flux during the whole no-load closing process. Under the premise of considering the different remanence, the scheme analyzes the tuning method of the voltage amplitude control parameters and the closing angle. A three-phase transformer no-load closing model is built to simulate the proposed method. The simulation results are compared with the direct closing scheme and phase-selection closing scheme. It show that the proposed method can be applied to all kinds of no-load closing situations and has better suppression effect of inrush current.

Author Keywords: integrated control of closing voltage parameters

articleTitle: An Advance Index to Evaluate the Stability of MMC-HVDC and Offshore Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Now, the modular multi-level converter high voltage direct current transmission(MMC-HVDC) is the most reliable solution for the long distance of the high voltage level transmission system. And the wind power is extensively used in the whole world, which is the most effective way to replace traditional power generation. In this paper, the advanced inertia response will be used to evaluate the stability of the MMC-HVDC system which connects with wind power. Then this method also can evaluate the transient characteristics of stability of the wind power and MMC-HVDC system. The simulation is divided into two parts: first, the simulation proceeds under normal conditions as the effective short circuit ratio(ESCR) increases. Second, the simulation has proceeded under the transient state which the AC side occurs the fault. This effectiveness of the scheme will be verified based on the simulation results of PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Transformer Winding Deformation Detection and Fault Identification Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The traditional detecting methods of winding deformation are off-line detection, and can not identify the winding deformation mode. This paper proposed a new transformer winding deformation detection method based on distributed optical fiber sensing. A fiber-optical composite winding model was designed, the influence of optical fiber on the electric field in oil was simulated, and a transformer winding model with built-in optical fiber was developed. The typical deformations of the transformer were set, using Brillouin optical time domain reflectometry (BOTDR) to measure the strain change of the fiber. Finally, the detection signal was pattern-recognized by the extreme learning machine (ELM). According to the results, the accuracy of ELM was more than 94% for different deformation forms. The distributed optical fiber sensing technology can detect the transformer winding deformation effectively, which provides a new approach for online monitoring of transformer winding deformation.

articleTitle: A Novel Protection Method of Wind Farm Collector Line Based on FCM Clustering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper presents a protection scheme based on cluster analysis for wind farm collector line. Since the short circuit current is related to the voltage sags, after the rotor Crowbar protection is put into operation during the short circuit fault of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG). There are three components in stator fault current which are taken as the fault feature. The fault information under different operating states are collected to form historical sample set. The cluster center of historical fault data was calculated to analyze fault data under different fault conditions by using cluster algorithm. The real-time sample categories are analyzed by distance similarity to achieve protection judgment. A detailed model of wind farm is built in DIgSILENT. The simulation results show that this method can solve the problem of selective loss of coordination and speed-up of protection for collector line in wind farm.

articleTitle: Influence Study of VSC-HVDC Interconnection on AC Line Differential Protection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: VSC-HVDC can improve the stability of AC grid, but it also changes the fault characteristics of AC grid. Thus, it is necessary to re-verify the AC line protection connected with VSC-HVDC. Based on the different operation modes of VSC-HVDC, the fault characteristics on VSC-HVDC system are analyzed: The magnitude of positive and negative sequence fault current is greatly influenced by VSC-HVDC control strategy and the negative sequence fault current is completely suppressed, but the zero sequence fault current characteristics are not affected. Based on the derived fault characteristics, an optimization strategy of starting elements is proposed, which is based on AC strong fault side commanding VSC-HVDC weak fault side and voltage reduction criterion. Meanwhile, the influence range of VSC-HVDC interconnection on fault characteristics of AC lines is given. Finally, a simulation model is built in PASCAD/EMTDC software and the effectiveness of the proposed optimization strategy is validated.

articleTitle: A Novel Topology of Hybrid DC Fault Current Limiter base on novel fault current limitation theory for DC Line Short Fault in HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Compared with the traditional AC power transmission system, the short-circuit current of HVDC grid dc side do not has natural zero-crossing, rises rapidly and is larger. Fault current limitation problem has become one of the major effects which constrain the development of high voltage DC transmission network. The most of existing current limitation theory is changing the impedance of DC transmission line by switching on some resistors or inductors in DC transmission line. In this paper, the proposed FCL reduce input voltage of limit current circuit of FCL by chopped wave technique and enhance ability of limit current of inductor by push-pull principle. Compared to other DC current limiters, This FCL not only limit rising rate of fault current in higher efficiency but also can limit the peak of fault current. The operation principle and limit theory is demonstrated in detail.

articleTitle: An Amplitude Comparison Protection for Distribution Networks with High Permeability Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Generations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For distribution networks with high-permeability inverter-interfaced distributed generations (IIDGs), the fault characteristics of IIDG are firstly analyzed, then, a method for analyzing the maximum short-circuit current that can be provided by IIDGs in active distribution network is proposed. Furthermore, a novel integrated current amplitude protection principle is proposed by comparing the two ends of the line positive phase current amplitude which achieves low-cost and high-reliability compatibility. The model of 10kV active distribution network was built by PSCAD to comprehensively simulate the influence of different DG permeability, fault type, transition resistance and other factors on the protection principle. After theoretical analysis and simulation, it is proved that the scheme can accurately solve the fault location problems, the data used is simple, the resistance to transition resistance is excellent, and the ability of resisting synchronization error is strong.

articleTitle: Damping Torque Analysis of the Influence of Different Types of Dead Band on Ultra-low Frequency Oscillation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The asynchronous interconnection between Yunnan Power Grid and the main grid of China Southern Power Grid has brought a series of frequency stability problems to the main grid of China Southern Power Grid. In the asynchronous network test in Yunnan and the subsequent DC blocking fault, two forms of frequency oscillation appear in the power grid. One type of oscillation is the divergence oscillation occurring near the rated frequency (f=50Hz), and Another type of oscillation occurs in the vicinity of the governor dead band (f = 0.05 Hz). In this paper, the causes of these two forms of oscillation are analyzed. When comparing the effects of different types of dead band, it is found that different types of governor dead band have different effects on the same input signal. Different output signals are analyzed by Fourier analysis method, and then analyzed by damping torque method. It is concluded that the two types of dead band have different amplitude reduction effects on the mechanical power of the system, which affects the system damping size and stable operation. And in the modified four-machine two-zone system model for time domain simulation, the results also prove the above conclusions.

articleTitle: Medium and Long Term Daily Load Forecasting Based on Boot-Feibes and Lisman Disaggregation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Medium and long term load forecasting is important for power system planning and optimization. To solve the problems of extra-long time span and heavy fluctuations in mid-long term load forecasting, a new daily load forecasting method is proposed in this paper, which can make fully use of the big data of economy, meteorology and electricity. Firstly, to address the issue of inaccuracy during holidays, a new method to depict the Spring Festival effect on a daily scale is proposed. Then, the quarterly GDP is expanded to daily level by Boot-Feibes and Lisman disaggregation (BFL), so that the time scale of economy and daily load is consistent. Finally, a support vector machine-based forecasting model is established to predict daily electricity consumption. The model is tested using the load data of a certain province in China. The results show that the proposed model outperforms other existing models, which is suitable for mid-long term daily load forecasting with complex influential factors.

articleTitle: Study on Power Supply Mode of Distribution Network Based on Three-phase to Single-phase AC_DC_AC Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: With the development of distribution network, the three-phase unbalance caused by increasingly complex loads affects the safety and economic operation of the power grid. For solving three-phase unbalanced problem, the power supply mode of the distribution network based on the three-phase to single-phase ac/dc/ac converter is proposed in this paper. A control method of a three-phase to single-phase ac/dc/ac converter is given, this power supply mode is evaluated from the aspects of equipment reliability, investment and construction cost, operation and maintenance cost and power quality. A distribution network power supply module based on three-phase to single-phase ac/dc/ac converter is implemented in PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results show that the proposed power supply method is feasible and has good reference for the planning and construction of distribution network.

articleTitle: Integration Control Strategy of IPOS DC Step-up Type Photovoltaic Power Plant Via MMC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Large-scale photovoltaic power plants use DC-collective boosting and delivery methods to have certain advantages in terms of transmission efficiency, cost and stability. This paper based on the scheme which the large-scale photovoltaic power station with input parallel output series (IPOS) is DC-boosted and then the modular multi-level single-ended flexible DC grid-connected, which deeply considers the voltage equalization and current sharing in the DC boost structure. To solve the problem, a DC-boost converter dynamic output voltage compensation control is combined with an optimized decoupling dual synchronous reference coordinate system phase-locked loop (DDSRF-PLL) for positive and negative sequence dual current loop control. Through the coordination between the pre-stage and the post-stage, the influence of the over-voltage and negative-sequence components of the DC bus on the grid-connected current is effectively suppressed. In addition, a soft start control strategy is proposed to suppress the system from overcurrent. Finally, the effectiveness of the control strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Turbine Location Wind Speed Forecast Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Traditional wind speed forecast usually regards wind farm as a point to make forecast, but in a wind farm, wind speed of wind turbines in different geographical locations is not the same. For many wind turbines with wide geographical distribution in a wind farm, this paper gives a forecast method based on convolutional neural network (CNN) to forecast the wind speed at each wind turbine location. In this method, the wind speed and direction characteristics of all wind turbines at different geographical locations are input into the CNN network as variables, and local low-dimensional features of the original data are mapped to high-dimensional features through convolution operation of CNN, thereby realizing the wind speed forecast. The main advantage of this method is that by automatically studying the informative spatial correlation of wind speed, rather than artificial extracting , multi-task forecasts(MTF)are made and the wind speed forecast at different wind turbines locations is more informative and accurate.

articleTitle: Research on the sampling reliability of process layer device in smart substation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: The double A/D sampling circuit is applied in the traditional substation to improve the reliability of relay equipment. In the process layer, the double A/D sampling circuit of the smart substation have differences with the traditional substation, the malfunction of relay protection is possibility caused by the abnormal operation of a single component. In this paper, by analyzing the structure of the smart substation sampling circuit, the weaknesses of sampling circuit in the smart substation would be found out. This paper points out two hardware redundancy design methods and analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of these two methods. The application of these two methods could solve the malfunction of relay protection device which is caused by the damage of single component in smart substation.

articleTitle: Nataf Transformation based Probabilistic Energy Flow Calculation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Since there exist various uncertainties in integrated energy systems, it is necessary to study the probabilistic energy flow of the integrated energy system. However, the existing probabilistic energy flow calculation methods have the problem of low computational efficiency and are difficult to add correlation between variables. This paper presents a calculation method to solve these probabilistic energy flow problems. First, this paper models the integrated energy system which is interconnected with natural gas and electricity system, and takes the uncertainty of wind farms and photovoltaic power plants in power system into account by carrying out Monte Carlo simulation. Second, this paper adds correlation between wind farm and photovoltaic power plants samples by Nataf transformation. Finally, time-domain simulations are performed, and the results show the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Voltage Sag Suppression Technique based on CLR and Artificial Current Zero Interruption of FVCB
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Voltage sag suppression technique based on based on current limiting reactor(CLR) and artificial current zero interruption technique of fast vacuum circuit breaker(FVCB) is proposed. The voltage sag suppression module is composed of FVCB, current limiting reactor and artificial zero crossing branch in parallel. In normal operation the FVCB is closed. A single break of 12-kV vacuum interrupter(VI) is used in the FVCB. A electromagnetic repulsion actuator is used to provide an opening velocity of 6.5 m/s and a closing velocity of 3.0 m/s. When a voltage sag happens, short-circuit current flows through the FVCB and the FVCB immediately opens within 0.5 ms, after 2.5 ms the artificial zero crossing branch generates a inverse-phase high-frequency current to make the arc extinguishing. After that the short-circuit current flows through the current limiting reactor so the amplitude of short-circuit current is limited and the bus voltage is well maintained. The over-voltage generated during interruption is suppressed by a group of ZnO surge arrestors.

articleTitle: Identification of Vulnerable Links in Power Grid Based on Brittleness Theory of Complex System under Geomagnetic Storm Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Geomagnetic disturbances will induce GIC (Geomagnetically Induced Currents) in high voltage power grid. GIC can cause cascading failure in power system, resulting in power system collapse or blackouts. In this paper, the mechanism of cascading failure in power system under geomagnetic storm is analyzed, and a vulnerable link identification process based on brittleness theory of complex system under geomagnetic storms is proposed. The brittleness theory of complex system is used to identify the vulnerable link and cascading failure propagating process of power grid under the condition of geomagnetic storm. Finally, the proposed process is validated by using the IEEE-RTS79 system. The verification results show the validity and practicability of the proposed process. The obtained results can provide reference for quantifying and preventing the risk of power grid under geomagnetic storms.

articleTitle: A Line Fault Type Detection Method Based on Optimal Sample Training Support Vector Machine in MMC-HVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Accurately identifying the type of line fault in the MMC-HVDC system is important for the fast recovery of the faulty line. However, high-resistance grounding faults have always been difficult to identify. This paper proposes a fault detection method based on Support Vector Machine (SVM).This method uses Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to extract several high-frequency intrinsic mode functions (IMF) from the fault voltage signal. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is used to find the optimal weight of each IMF and reconstruct the waveform signal as the feature of different line faultes to train SVM classification model.This paper establishes a ± 250kV MMC-HVDC simulation model to verify the test results.The simulation results verify that the SVM model trained by the optimized samples can accurately identify different types of line faults by low sampling frequency and fewer fault waveform sampling points.

articleTitle: Assessment of Wind Power Ramp Events Based on Stacked Denoising Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Wind power ramp events had a significant impact on the power balance of power system and may lead to load shedding. A data driven method was proposed for wind power ramp events assessment in this paper. The K-means clustering algorithm was used to divide the samples to several classes. The stacked denoising autoencoder was used to extract layer features to train support vector machine. Historical and forecast data of wind power, load power, conventional unit and pumped storage station power were taken as inputs. The output was whether ramp event occurred. A severity function was constructed to assess the severity grade which was predicted to be a wind power ramp event based on effect theory. The credibility of the assessment result was represented by confidence interval. Simulation results of a provincial power grid showed that the prediction method in this paper was more accurate and credibility was high enough to help the dispatchers to take measures for the security of power grid.

articleTitle: Distribution networks ground fault protection method based on fuzzy measure fusion criterion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for ground fault protection of distribution networks based on fuzzy measure fusion criterion. The fuzzy c-means clustering algorithm is used to characterize the historical characteristics of different operating states of protected feeders under various operating conditions. The sample set is divided into fault class and non-fault class. The sample similarity measure criterion is used to quantitatively analyze the similarity degree between the sample to be tested and different types of historical samples, forming a fuzzy measure fusion criterion matrix, and fuzzy by multi-level evaluation index system. The measurement fusion criterion matrix is used to judge, and finally a comprehensive criterion matrix is output as the protection criterion. The simulation results of PSCAD/EMTDC show that under the influence of non-linear load and other disturbance factors, the method can still accurately identify fault samples and is not affected by changes in system operation mode, and has strong robustness.

articleTitle: Influence of DC Current Flowing through the Ground Electrode on AC Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Under the condition of the unipolar operation, the earthing current of DC ground electrode will cause distortion in earth surface potential (ESP), having adverse impacts on the surrounding environment and AC power grid. This paper uses the finite element method (FEM) to analyze ESP distribution, and the influence of currents and geoelectric parameters on the ESP distribution is taken into account. Taking Qilian converter station as an example, the DC equivalent model of Gansu grid is established to simulate the bias current in the power system around the ground electrode. Results show that the ESP distribution is greatly affected by the soil structure, and the bias level of transformers is related to the grid structure and the distance between stations and the ground electrode. The transformer with DC bias is mainly concentrated in regions close to the ground electrode, providing a reference for the treatment and prevention of bias current.

articleTitle: Fault location of UHV DC transmission line based on variational mode decomposition and energy operator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Traveling wave fault location is widely used because it isn't affected by transition resistance and operation mode, but it is difficult to accurately and effectively detect the arrival time of fault traveling wave head in the early stage of fault occurrence. In view of this, a traveling wave head detection method based on the combination of variational mode decomposition and Teager energy operator is proposed. Firstly, the acquired fault traveling wave signal is decomposed into variational modes, and then the most sensitive IMF component is demodulated by Teager energy operator. The energy spectrum of the fault traveling wave signal is obtained. The first obvious mutation point in the energy spectrum is the arrival time of the first wave head of the fault traveling wave. The simulation results show that the location error of this method doesn't exceed ±0.2% of the actual fault distance, which proves the feasibility of the principle.

articleTitle: Internal Fault Characteristics and Optimized Main Protection Configuration for Asymmetric Winding Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For the design of large hydro-generator with perfect paralleled-branches number and rated speed, the asymmetric windings are more widely adopted nowadays. Due to the special connection of the armature winding, the fault characteristics of the internal short-circuits in the asymmetric winding are different from those of the conventional symmetrical winding. Taking the 4-branches asymmetric winding generator for an example, the characteristics of all the possible internal faults are analyzed in detail, and the fault currents distribution is calculated with the multi-loop method.
