Then the optimized protection configuration is obtained in the nonadjacent branchgrouping mode of the generator, composed of the split-phase transverse differential protection, complete longitudinal differential protection and zero-sequence current transverse differential protection. Comparing with another scheme shows that, the operation rate and the double-protection rate of the optimized scheme meet a high technical standard. The results in this paper could guide the design of main protection configuration for other generators with asymmetric windings.

articleTitle: A fault line selection method based on zero-mode components
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: To solve the problems of fault line selection in resonant grounding system, a novel fault line selection method for distribution network was proposed in this paper. This method based on transient zero-mode differential current and signal distance algorithm. Firstly, the transient zero-mode differential current is proposed to distinguish between bus fault and branch fault by the zero-mode network analysis of single-phase grounded transient zero-mode current characteristics. Then, based on the signal distance algorithm, the fault line selection vector is constructed to determine the fault branch. The fault line is determined by the minimum element. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed method is not affected by fault initial angle, fault resistance and network structure, which improves the accuracy of fault line selection.

articleTitle: Commutation Failure Mitigation Method Based on Improved Commutation Area in HVDC system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: Commutation failure (CF) is one of the major concerns in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system. Of many methods to mitigate CF, advancing firing angle is preferred one since it can be easily implemented in current HVDC controllers without extra hardware modification. However, methods in previous works either lack for quantitative analysis or based on much strong hypothesis. In this paper, we propose a novel CF mitigation method based on improved commutation area. The salient feature of proposed strategy is that DC current is not considered as a constant under fault conditions. Simulations on PSCAD/EMTDC software demonstrate the good performance of proposed method.

articleTitle: Sampling Synchronization Method Using Power System Modeling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: For the line differential protection relays, sampling synchronization is one of the most critical factors to affect the protection performance. Previously, sampling synchronization using voltage phase difference was proposed. In this paper, simulations for more complex, but actually existing, systems such as transmission line consisting of underground cable and over-head line and three-terminal line are carried out. The proposed method is applicable for two-terminal line even if the line consisting of underground cable and over-head line. However, for three (or more) -terminal line, the simple model, which is able to calculate in the relay, may have some error for synchronization and then, this method is only applicable for the limited system.

articleTitle: Harmonics Frequencies Impedance Estimation Based on Least-square method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to estimate the grid impedance at fundamental as well as harmonics frequencies. The required measurements are voltage and current at the point of common coupling (PCC) under normal operating conditions. The source voltages are also estimated simultaneously. The estimation method is based on Least Squares (LS), using the Orthogonality Principle in complex Hilbert space to deal with complex variables directly. By simulations, the influence of measurements noise on the estimation accuracy at fundamental and harmonic frequencies is investigated in detail.

articleTitle: Application of Transfer Entropy Algorithm in Fault Detection for Power System with Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE 8th International Conference on Advanced Power System Automation and Protection (APAP)
abstract: As the controllability of power electronic devices associated with wind turbines leads to a variety of fault characteristics, fault detection for power system with wind turbine has become a serious challenge. The theory of information entropy can quantify the degree of system uncertainty which has achieved good application results in the field of feature extraction and fault detection for power system. This paper proposed a solution to detect faults through transfer entropy algorithm. Firstly, the fundamentals of the algorithm is introduced. Then the algorithm is implemented on the field testing data of wind turbine fault ride through, and the details of parameter optimization is described. Finally, the adaptability of transfer entropy is studied considering different wind turbine capacities, controller models and different grid faults. This study provides theoretical and practical basis for the application of transfer entropy algorithm in the field of feature extraction and fault detection for power system.
